monument_name: Dharma Gaddi statues and stone memorial pillar
anglicized_name: Dharma Gaddi statues and stone memorial pillar
name_devanagari: धर्म गद्दी मूर्तिहरू र खम्बा || DLK0200
description_en: A recently built roofed platform housing stone artefacts from the medieval and modern period.The platform is located at the centre of the locality of Dullu, to the south of the now destroyed royal palace of the Dullu kings.In the late 1990's, the site merely consisted in a hypaethral platform, receiving shadow from a large tree. Stone sculptures were placed on a small altar made of bricks. The platform was cemented and enlarged after the destruction of the royal palace by Maoists in 2002 (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009: p. 274, fn. 73). Later some wooden posts were added and a roof of metal sheets was installed. Furthermore, a wall was built to the northern side of the platform. Some of the stone images were set in niches arranged for them.There are several sculptures in the round and in high relief of Buddhist and Hindu affiliations. Of note are a few Buddhist deities: a broken Buddha (DLK0200-003), a Saḍakṣarī Lokeśvara (?, (DLK0200-002), and the bust of a potential Avalokiteśvara (DLK0200-007). Another sculpture, also identified as Avalokiteśvara is placed in a niche (DLK0200-005). The face of the figure, seated on a column in a "royal position of ease", has been deliberately damaged. All the Buddhist sculptures show signs of iconoclastic vandalism. The condition of the so-called Avalokiteśvara bust and the Avalokiteśvara seated on the column would therefore tend to identify them as Buddhist figures. The presence of Buddhism in this place is also attested by an inscribed but illegible stele decorated with an incised stūpa at the top (DLK0200-001). A stele of Viṣṇu and Lakṣmī, meanwhile, shows no marks of vandalism (Andolfatto 2019: p. 166). According to P. R. Sharma the so-called bust of Avalokiteśvara (DLK0200-007) was installed (in 1967) in "Dullu Bhairavathan", which is a small temple south of Dharma Gaddi (Sharma 1972: p. 28). D. R. Sharma proposes to date this sculpture from the 11th century (Sharma 2012: p. 40).The artefacts may be roughly dated from the 12th to the 19th century.
description_ne: दैलेखको दुल्लुमा अवस्थित यस स्मारकस्थलमा मध्यकालदेखि आधुनिककालसम्मका पाषाण मूर्ति तथा स्तम्भ रहेका छन् । दुल्लुको केन्द्रमा रहेको यस स्मारकस्थल हाल भग्न अवस्थामा रहेको दुल्लु राजाहरूका दरवारको दक्षिणमा पर्दछ ।सन् ९० को दशकको उत्तरार्द्धसम्म पनि छाना बिनाको यस स्मारकस्थल एक ठूलो रूखको छायाँमा रहेको थियो । यहाँ रहेका ढुंगाका मूर्तिहरू ईट्टाले बनाइएको वेदीमा राखिएका थिए । सन् २००२ मा माओवादीले दरवार ध्वस्त बनाइदिए पछि सो वेदीमा सिमेन्ट लगाई विस्तार गरिएको थियो (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009: p. 274, fn. 73) । पछि यस स्थललाई काठका थाम ठड्याई जस्तापाताले छोपिएको थियो । वेदीको उत्तरतिर गारो लगाई केही मूर्तिहरू गवाक्षहरूमा राखियो ।यहाँ थुप्रै बौद्ध र हिन्दू मूर्तिहरू रहेका छन् । ती मध्ये टुक्रिएको बुद्ध मूर्ति (DLK0200-003), षडक्षरी लोकेश्वर (DLK0200-002) र अर्धकदको अवलोकितेश्वर (DLK0200-007) को जस्तो देखिने मूर्तिहरू छन् । अवलोकितेश्वरकै अर्को एक मूर्ति गवाक्षमा राखिएको छ (DLK0200-005) । यस मूर्तिको अनुहार नियोजित रूपमै फुटाइएको देखिन्छ । यहाँ रहेका सबै बौद्ध मूर्तिहरू तोडफोडको शिकार भएको देखिन्छ । यहाँ बुद्ध धर्मको उपस्थिति रहेको कुरा चैत्यको चित्र कुँदिएको एक स्तम्भ अभिलेखबाट पनि स्पष्ट हुन्छ (DLK0200-001) । हाल सो अभिलेख पढ्न सकिने अवस्थामा भने छैन । विष्णु र लक्ष्मीको मूर्तिमा भने कुनै क्षति पुर्‍याइएको छैन (Andolfatto 2019:p.166) । अवलोकितेश्वरको अर्धकदको मूर्ति (DLK0200-007) पहिले यस धर्मगद्दीको दक्षिणमा पर्ने भैरवस्थानमा सन् १९६७ मा राखिएको थियो (Sharma 1972:p.28) । सो मूर्ति ११ औं शताव्दीको हो (Sharma 2012: p. 40) ।यहाँ रहेको विभिन्न मूर्ति तथा स्तम्भ १२ औं देखि १९ औं शताव्दीमा बनाइएको अनुमान गर्न सकिन्छ ।
